newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CEZ pursues dividend battle with ministry.
newsitem.headline: CEZ pursues dividend battle with ministry.

text.p: A battle between the Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade and electrical utility CEZ a.s. over the firm's intention to pay its first-ever dividend is threatening to spill into its annual meeting next Thursday.
CEZ's board initially proposed a 1996 dividend totalling three percent of each 1,100 crown nominally-valued share, though it later lowered its demand to two percent.
"The board remains with its scheme. Originally it was to be three percent, though we have lowered it to two. What the ministry will come up with still isn't clear," said CEZ spokesman Ladislav Kriz.
The ministry, which controls a 68 percent stake in CEZ, says it is still not satisfied with the proposal and would prefer a continuation of CEZ's no dividend policy.
"With an outlook on the firm's results and the development of electricity prices, (the ministry) does not support this proposal," said senior ministry official Ivan Novak.
With the battle lines drawn, shareholders are caught in the middle. The AGM is on June 19 and any dividend payment will be made according to shareholders registered as of June 12.
Both Kriz and Novak said that if an agreement cannot be reached before the AGM, both proposals will be submitted to shareholders.
According to Czech accounting standards, CEZ posted a 1996 net profit of 7.85 billion crowns, down from 8.06 billion the year before.

Net profit was originally expected to fall to 6.1 billion crowns in 1997, but the firm has said reduced revenues as demand weakens due to a slowing economy may take as much as one billion crowns more off CEZ's bottom line.
"The firm needs to gather the maximum possible funds for its development needs," said ministry spokeswoman Zuzana Fialova.
